recall.answer: U06 · Pretraining, scaling, systems, data.
recall.question: What unit is this?

keyTerms.definition: Cross-entropy on one token. Pretraining losses are means of this number.
About 77 tokens per sequence carry the MLM loss. The rest are context.
Byte arithmetic: fp16 = 2 bytes, fp32 = 4 bytes per number.

recall.answer: About 77. 15 percent of 512 is 76.8.
recall.question: How many tokens carry the MLM loss per 512-sequence?

keyTerms.definition: The masking recipe: the task, plus robustness against trusting the mask.
Predict masked tokens from full bidirectional context.

recall.answer: 0.487 at p(true) = 0.614. One token, one loss.
recall.question: What was the toy masked loss?

recall.answer: Fine-tuning has no masks: a train/test skew. The recipe exists because of this failure.
recall.question: Why not 100% [MASK]?

keyTerms.definition: AR’s signal-per-pass advantage over MLM at n = 512.
The AR loss: P(w_t | prefix) for every t. No masks, no recipes.

recall.answer: Mean over t of -log P(w_t | w_<t). n predictions per sequence of length n.
recall.question: What is the AR loss?

recall.answer: No. Early AR models underperformed MLM on understanding benchmarks at small scale.
recall.question: Does more signal mean better models?

keyTerms.definition: The layer output at a position: a function of the whole sequence.
Same-sense cos 0.998, cross-sense 0.424 for “bank”.

recall.answer: Same-sense 0.998, cross-sense 0.424. Context moves the vector more than word identity.
recall.question: What were the toy cosines?

recall.answer: On tiny data: fewer parameters, less overfitting. Context is capacity, it needs data.
recall.question: When does static beat contextual?

keyTerms.definition: Filtering, dedup, mixing, decontamination: each a judgment call with measurable effect.
Hash the normalized text, keep first occurrence. Duplicates waste capacity and leak.

recall.answer: 6 docs, 3 exact duplicates, 3 unique. Half the toy corpus was waste.
recall.question: What was the toy dedup result?

recall.answer: It displaces good tokens. Quality per FLOP beats bytes.
recall.question: Why does adding bad data hurt at fixed compute?

keyTerms.definition: The compute budget: 6 FLOPs per param per token.
The compute-optimal tokens-per-param ratio from the scaling literature.

recall.answer: N = 1e8, D = 2e9: C = 1.20e18 FLOPs, 20.0 tokens/param.
recall.question: What was the toy budget?

recall.answer: Inference favors big models on fewer tokens: a deployment tradeoff.
recall.question: Why are most published models undertrained by this ratio?

keyTerms.definition: A ruler, not a crystal ball. L = a N^{-b}; predicts the next point, not the next paradigm.
2^{-b}: a 3.4 percent loss cut per doubling at b = 0.05.

recall.question: What were the four fitted values?

recall.answer: Data exhaustion, architecture changes, emergent jumps: the law is about loss, not capabilities.
recall.question: What breaks the law?

keyTerms.definition: Averages gradients across workers. The tax: 2(p-1)/p x size per step.
Bounded: approaches 2S as p grows.

recall.answer: p = 8, S = 1 GB -> 1.75 GB/step. Noise 1.026 -> 0.0299 at batch 32.
recall.question: What was the toy tax?

recall.answer: Small batches make communication dominate. The speedup stalls.
recall.question: Why scale the batch with p?

keyTerms.definition: Decide the rule before training, publish it with the model card.
A benchmark question appears verbatim in training; the benchmark measures recall.

recall.answer: 2.9 points: reported 45% vs clean 42.1%.
recall.question: What did the leak buy?

recall.answer: Benchmark text is duplicated across the web. Big data contains more copies, not fewer.
recall.question: Why does scale increase the risk?

keyTerms.definition: Freeze the body, train a linear head. Measures feature quality.
Lower layers learn reusable features; the task head learns the decision.

recall.answer: 92% vs 55% baseline. The gap is the transfer, measured.
recall.question: What was the toy probe gap?

recall.answer: Pretraining on the wrong domain can hurt: the body must unlearn.
recall.question: What does negative transfer mean?

keyTerms.definition: Data provenance, training recipe, evaluation scope, known limits, in one place.
Identity, data, training, evaluation, limitations, use. Facts, not adjectives.

recall.answer: toy-1e8: AR, N=1e8, D=2e9, C=1.20e18. Web mix, exact-deduped, decontaminated vs bench-X. Held-out ppl 36.2.
recall.question: What was the toy card?

recall.answer: Papers describe the idea; cards describe the artifact. Different documents, both needed.
recall.question: Paper vs card?

keyTerms.definition: Did it learn the distribution, what is in the representations, what it can do.
Leaked held-out NLL 3.10 (ppl 22.2) vs clean 36.2. Report all three or nothing.

recall.answer: Train 30.0, held-out 36.2, leaked-held-out 22.2.
recall.question: What were the three perplexities?

recall.answer: Perplexity without provenance is a number without meaning.
recall.question: What does 22.2 < 30.0 prove?

keyTerms.definition: The 100B training memory stack. No single GPU holds it.
Data-parallel + tensor-parallel + pipeline-parallel. FSDP shards all three states.

recall.answer: 1.2 TB / 32 GPUs = 37.5 GB each (plus activations).
recall.question: What was the sharded result?

recall.answer: At small models: the allgather adds communication per layer. Shard only what does not fit.
recall.question: When is FSDP slower than data-parallel?

keyTerms.definition: Mask 15 percent, predict the masked: the MLM plate.
Power-law form: doubling cuts loss 3.4 percent.

recall.answer: Mask plate (MLM), power-law plate (doubling cuts 3.4%), memory stack (Adam states dominate).
